title: Enterprise Private & Hybrid-Cloud AI Landing Zone Architecture Selection

tiers.tier: Tier 1: Public Internet SaaS LLM Endpoints Without Private Link or Data Classification
tiers.architecture: Sending all enterprise data levels (L1 Public through L4 Restricted Core Secrets) over public internet NAT to SaaS APIs

tiers.tier: Tier 2: 100% Air-Gapped On-Premises Physical GPU Data Center for All Workloads (`L1–L4`)
tiers.architecture: Buying 64x on-premises H100 servers (`$2.4M CapEx`) to run 100% of company AI workloads (including L1/L2 public marketing & coding)

tiers.tier: Tier 3: Cloud Private Link Only While Pulling On-Premises Core Databases Over WAN Per Query
tiers.architecture: Cloud LLM via Private Endpoint, but every RAG/Agent call queries on-premises mainframes/databases synchronously across WAN

tiers.tier: Tier 4: Data-Classified Hybrid AI Landing Zone (`On-Prem / Azure Arc vLLM` for 20% `L4 Secret` + `ExpressRoute Private Link` Cloud AI for 80% `L1–L3`)
tiers.architecture: Sensitivity-Aware AI Gateway routes 20% L4 Regulated/Crown-Jewel data to local On-Premises / Confidential GPUs (`8x H200`) and 80% L1–L3 workloads over ExpressRoute/DirectConnect Private Link + CMK Zero-Data-Retention Cloud AI

scenarios.scenario: Avoiding the '$2.4M All-On-Premises GPU CapEx Trap' via L1–L4 Data-Sensitivity Routing
scenarios.question: A defense/financial enterprise states 'Our core customer ledger (L4) cannot leave our on-premises data center,' so IT proposes buying 64x H100s on-premises for all 25,000 employees
scenarios.model_answer: Audit actual workload data sensitivity: only **15%–20% of enterprise AI prompts touch `L4 Restricted / Crown-Jewel` records**, while **80%–85% touch `L1–L3` data** (code assistance, HR policies, public market research, internal SOPs). Size a compact **8x H200 On-Premises / Azure Arc K8s cluster** strictly for the 20% L4 traffic, and route the 80% L1–L3 traffic over **ExpressRoute + Private Link** to Cloud AI with Customer-Managed Keys (`CMK`) and Zero Data Retention (`$68K/mo` vs `$238K/mo` all-on-prem, -71.4%)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 2 buys 64 on-premises GPUs (6-month hardware lead time + data center power/cooling retrofit) just to run L1/L2 office summarization (`62.5%` idle hardware waste).

scenarios.scenario: Eliminating the 1,890ms 'Cross-WAN RAG Ping-Pong' Between Cloud LLMs and On-Premises Databases
scenarios.question: When a Cloud LLM Agent executes 5 sequential tool/RAG lookups against an on-premises Oracle/DB2 database over WAN, network round-trips add 1.5 seconds of latency
scenarios.model_answer: Deploy **Data-Gravity Co-Location**: keep the L4 RAG vector index and local `vLLM` inference node co-located inside the on-premises data center next to Oracle/DB2 (`290ms` P95 latency), and replicate only sanitized/tokenized L1–L3 read projections to the Cloud Landing Zone via CDC (`Kafka / MirrorMaker`)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 3 performs 5 synchronous cross-WAN SQL/vector round-trips per turn (`1,890ms` P95 latency).

scenarios.scenario: Hub-and-Spoke Private AI Landing Zone (`Private Endpoint + DNS Forwarding + Zero Public Egress`)
scenarios.question: How do we guarantee that cloud-hosted AI workloads (`Azure AI Foundry / AWS Bedrock`) never traverse the public internet or get logged for provider model training?
scenarios.model_answer: Provision a Hub-and-Spoke Cloud AI Landing Zone: disable public network access on all AI/Search/Storage resources, bind `Azure Private Link / AWS PrivateLink` interfaces into the Spoke VNet connected via `ExpressRoute / Direct Connect`, enforce `Customer-Managed Keys (CMK / HSM)`, and enable Enterprise **Zero Data Retention (Abuse Monitoring Opt-Out)** (`100.0%` sovereignty compliance)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 routes prompts over public internet NAT gateways without Private Link or abuse-monitoring opt-out (`0.0%` L4 compliance).

scenarios.scenario: Unified Control Plane Across On-Premises and Cloud Kubernetes (`Azure Arc / EKS Anywhere + GitOps`)
scenarios.question: How does a 4-person platform team manage both on-premises GPU nodes and cloud endpoints without maintaining two completely different software stacks?
scenarios.model_answer: Manage on-premises GPU servers as an `Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes / EKS Anywhere / Anthos` cluster using a single GitOps (`ArgoCD / Flux`) control plane, unified `Envoy AI Gateway` routing policies, and shared `OpenTelemetry` observability
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 2 builds a bespoke snowflake on-premises stack that lags 9 months behind cloud model releases (`68.0%` capability coverage).

perturbation_checks.check: User Accidentally Pastes an `L4 Restricted` Secret Key / Core Ledger Row into an `L2` Cloud Copilot
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 100.0% Compliance (Inline Sensitivity Classifier at AI Gateway Intercepts L4 Classification Tag/Pattern & Re-Routes to On-Premises `vLLM` Automatically)

perturbation_checks.check: ExpressRoute / Direct Connect Primary Fiber Cut Between On-Premises DC and Cloud Region
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 315ms P95 Latency (Automatic BGP Failover to Secondary ExpressRoute Circuit + Local On-Premises `vLLM` Continuity for Critical L4 Ops)

key_findings: Tier 4 (Data-Classified Hybrid AI Landing Zone: 20% L4 Restricted on local 8x H200 On-Premises cluster + 80% L1–L3 on Cloud AI via ExpressRoute Private Link + CMK) achieves 100% sovereignty compliance and 99.2% frontier capability coverage at $68K/mo (-71.4% vs $238K/mo 100% air-gapped on-prem).
Sizing on-premises hardware for 100% of company traffic when only 20% of prompts touch L4 restricted data wastes 62.5% of CapEx on workloads that belong on elastic cloud infrastructure.
Co-locating L4 RAG vector indexes and local vLLM inference next to on-premises core databases eliminates the 1,890ms cross-WAN RAG ping-pong latency.
